key_insight: Machine-learned long-timescale simulations reveal that surface small-polaron motion on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) is drastically slower than in the bulk because hopping pathways are geometrically constrained at the surface.
engineering_relevance: This explains why porous rutile TiO2 can show much lower electron mobility than single-crystal material, informing the design of oxide-based catalysts, photoelectrodes, and energy-storage devices.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a redox-active oxide surface.
Ran several nanoseconds of finite-temperature dynamics on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110).
Compared surface and bulk hopping pathways and polaron distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nanosecond-scale simulations across temperatures and finds surface polaron mobility suppressed by several orders of magnitude relative to bulk, with rare interlayer hopping events and vacancy-driven localization near Ti sites.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110), so transferability to other oxides and defect chemistries still needs validation.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
